purpose: Plan context, not a contract interpreter or a provider-blame classifier.

providers.name: Contabo
providers.summary: Shared VPS and dedicated-resource VDS are different products. Match the actual purchased family before applying performance guidance.

facts.text: The VPS documentation describes shared virtual CPU cores. A newer CPU generation does not make the allocation dedicated.
The VDS product documentation describes CPU cores reserved for the instance. Its dedicated-core benchmark guidance is not a shared-VPS minimum.

check_next: Record the exact product family, plan and region.
Keep confirmed migration completion separate from an offer or scheduling reply.
Compare workload limits and service impact with repeated observations.
providers.not_a_promise: No numeric guest-accounted-time floor is established by these references. The skill's 90% and 80% levels are user preferences, not Contabo guarantees.
providers.support_question: Can you review host-side scheduling for this specific VM and UTC interval?

providers.name: Hetzner
providers.summary: Identify shared CX/CPX/CAX versus dedicated CCX. Keep the baseline/burst model and hardware generation in the comparison.

facts.text: Hetzner describes shared compute with a baseline and temporary bursting above it; resources are distributed among instances on a physical server.
Dedicated plans reserve CPU resources. Hetzner defines one vCPU as one thread of a physical core, not an entire processor.

check_next: Confirm the family and architecture rather than guessing from the hostname.
Distinguish a plan baseline from measured throughput.
Retain a comparable before/after window if the host or plan changes.
providers.not_a_promise: A baseline/burst description does not establish that every sample must exceed the skill's chosen tolerance.
providers.support_question: Does this interval reflect the expected allocation model for our purchased plan?

providers.name: DigitalOcean
providers.summary: Select the actual CPU allocation class. Premium hardware and dedicated CPU access are separate characteristics.

facts.text: Shared configurations share CPU access. They are intended for variable or bursty demand rather than continuously guaranteed compute.
The plan guide distinguishes dedicated CPU configurations for sustained workloads from shared configurations. Verify the selected family and generation.

check_next: Record the Droplet family and CPU allocation class.
Compare application latency, errors and workload concurrency over the same UTC range.
Do not treat Premium in a plan name as proof of dedicated allocation.
providers.not_a_promise: Uptime commitments and dedicated allocation are not identical to a guarantee for this guest accounting formula.
providers.support_question: Please help distinguish host-side contention from the expected behavior of this Droplet family.

providers.name: Akamai / Linode
providers.summary: The documented maximum sustained usage for shared CPU is an allowance, not a delivered-capacity floor.

facts.text: The comparison guide lists 80% maximum sustained CPU utilization and 100% burst utilization for shared plans. It also says contention can occur at peak usage.
The same guide describes reserved CPU resources and 100% sustained usage for dedicated plans.

check_next: Compare sustained demand to the applicable usage policy.
Do not convert the 80% usage allowance into an 80% CPU-delivery guarantee.
providers.not_a_promise: Maximum permitted utilization and measured delivered CPU time describe different quantities.
providers.support_question: Is our workload within the plan's sustained-use policy, and is the observed contention expected?

providers.name: AWS EC2
providers.summary: For burstable instances, inspect credits and Standard/Unlimited mode before attributing a slowdown to neighbors.

facts.text: CPU credits and the instance-size baseline govern bursting. Record CPUCreditBalance and the configured credit mode for the measured interval.
Unlimited can use surplus credits after the balance is depleted; sustained use above the baseline may incur additional charges. No price is assumed here.

check_next: Record instance type and Standard or Unlimited mode.
Review CPUCreditBalance, CPUCreditUsage and surplus-credit metrics in the authorized monitoring system.
Check system status, storage/network limits and the application's actual latency or errors separately.
providers.not_a_promise: A depleted balance or burst ceiling is not by itself proof of a noisy neighbor. This skill does not collect CloudWatch credits automatically.
providers.support_question: Can you help interpret this interval against the instance's credit mode, baseline and status checks?

providers.name: Other / not yet identified
providers.summary: Use the exact purchased plan and the provider's primary documentation. Do not borrow another supplier's threshold.
check_next: Identify the provider, product, CPU allocation model and current plan.
Save a dated link to product terms, usage limits and relevant support documentation privately.
Mark unknown terms as unknown until reviewed; do not infer a guarantee.
providers.not_a_promise: No contractual or usage policy is inferred for an unidentified product.
providers.support_question: What CPU allocation and sustained-use policy applies to this exact plan?
